reason: The narration describes a clear shift in location and function of the terracotta head—from lying in the earth for two and a half millennia, to being used as a scarecrow on a jackfruit garden for a year, to finally being recognized as a held object. These are distinct visual states requiring separate shots.

beats.visual_intent: A terracotta head lies buried in the soil, surrounded by earth and roots, with no human presence visible.
search_queries: ancient Chinese terracotta head in archaeological context
beats.edit: Static wide shot of a terracotta head half-buried in soil, showing erosion and age, with subtle wind and leaf movement.

beats.visual_intent: The same terracotta head is now placed on a garden plot, acting as a scarecrow, with a jackfruit tree growing nearby.
beats.edit: Medium shot of a terracotta head standing upright on a small garden, with a jackfruit tree in the background, wind gently blowing.

beats.visual_intent: A person is holding the terracotta head in their hands, looking at it with realization.
search_queries: someone discovering ancient artifact in hands
beats.edit: Close-up of hands gently cradling the terracotta head, with soft ambient light and a subtle background of a rural setting.
